title: Dock Rebalancing
headline: Empty docks fill themselves,
lede: A planner proposes van moves each morning. Dispatchers accept them one at a time, and riders see a reward for ending a trip at a dock that needs bikes.
notes: Two parts: the shared planner, then the two places people act on it. Ask for the three decisions at the end.

chapters.title: The shared planner
chapters.summary: One plan per morning, built from yesterday's trips and today's forecast.

sections.title: Rebalancing runs on a whiteboard and a radio
sections.lede: Dispatchers read dock counts off a map, write moves on a board and radio them to vans.

pains.title: Slow
pains.text: A move takes 6 minutes to decide and 40 to run, so it lands after the rush.

pains.title: Not auditable
pains.text: Nobody can say which moves helped; the board is wiped at noon.

sections.title: Five whys, from the empty dock to the root

rows.text: Docks near stations are empty from 08:10 to 09:30.
Vans arrive after the dock is empty, not before.
Moves are chosen from the live map, which only shows the present.
**No part of the system forecasts demand per dock, so no move can be planned ahead.**

sections.title: How we solve it
sections.thesis: Plan the moves the night before. We only need to ==forecast each dock== and ==let dispatch accept a plan==.
